notes.n2.merchant: NVIDIA dominates; AMD is the main merchant alternative, with Intel and Qualcomm targeting inference.
notes.n2.custom: Google, AWS, Microsoft, Meta and OpenAI all run in-house ASIC programmes, mostly co-designed with Broadcom, Marvell, MediaTek or Alchip.
notes.n2.startup: Consolidating fast: NVIDIA took Groq (licence and hires, Dec 2025) and Enfabrica, AMD took Untether AI's team (product discontinued Jun 2025), Cerebras listed (May 2026). Inference-focused challengers keep raising large rounds.
notes.n2.china: Export controls drove a 2025-26 IPO wave (Moore Threads, MetaX, Biren, Kunlunxin filing); Huawei Ascend and Cambricon lead.
notes.n2.edge: NPUs are now standard in phone/PC SoCs (Apple, Qualcomm, MediaTek, Intel, AMD); discrete edge players compete in vision, auto and industrial.
notes.n2.cpu: Arm-based custom CPUs (Grace, Graviton, Cobalt, Axion) are eroding x86 in AI head nodes; Ampere now owned by SoftBank.
notes.n2.net: Scale-up/scale-out fabrics are a battleground (NVLink vs UALink/Ultra Ethernet); photonics startups being absorbed (Celestial AI to Marvell, Enfabrica to NVIDIA).
notes.n2.sw: CUDA lock-in remains the main moat; ROCm, Triton, XLA and Modular push portability.
notes.n2.photonic: Consolidating: Marvell bought Celestial AI (closed Feb 2026), Ciena bought Nubis (2025)
notes.n2.power: NVIDIA 800 VDC programme lists 14 silicon partners (GTC 2026)
notes.n2.export: Compliance burden rose after BIS rescinded the AI Diffusion Rule and issued chip guidance (May 2025)
